summary: At the review date, only the Minimum Core Assets Test (C01) requires tightening to buffer against inventory overstatement risk shown by an $8M write-off of excess component inventory in Q4 2024. All other clauses (C02‑C05) are retained as no new evidence justifies change. This constitutes a material drift.

clauses.rationale: Evidence shows $8M write-off of excess component inventory in Q4 2024, indicating inventory management challenges that could overstate core assets and increase cash consumption.
clauses.change: Increase the Minimum Core Assets Test threshold to provide a buffer against potential inventory overstatement.

evidence.quote: Additionally, we recorded an incremental non-recurring charge in the fourth quarter of $8 million related to the write-off of excess component inventory and losses on non-cancelable purchase commitments

clauses.rationale: No evidence of financial statement delivery issues; assumption A06 supported.
Monthly reporting already includes inventory via balance sheets; no new evidence requiring change.
Amazon break fee has been received and used as per existing sweep; no evidence of need to alter.
No evidence of default notice issues; assumption unchanged.

drift_reasons: The tightened threshold for C01 addresses inventory overstatement risk evidenced by a Q4 2024 $8M write-off, altering risk coverage and thus constituting material drift.
